_comment: MODSET name->factor table for the production general-interval hook (frida/trampoline_inject.py, TTRMOD_MODE=modset). ONE install of the Python MetaInterval.start wrapper reads each started interval's getName() and setPlayRate's it with the factor of the FIRST matching entry -- so all cosmetic animation groups speed up at once, and nothing else is touched. factor = speed multiplier (3.0 = 3x faster / ~1/3 the duration). match = substring of the interval name (set prefix:true to anchor at the start instead). Entries are tried IN ORDER; put specific matches before broad ones. enabled:false stubs an entry out. Names matching NO entry are logged (log_unmatched) but never scaled, so gameplay-timing intervals stay intact. The interval NAMES are TTR's real ones (observed live via TTRMOD_LOGNAMES); the class is pinned per-build in trampoline_inject.py (META_INTERVAL_MODULE/CLASS) -- re-derive on an engine auto-patch.
_comment_context: The `context` section scales intervals by CREATION CONTEXT (a wrapped method sets a global flag; intervals that START during it are scaled), for a spawner that builds+starts its interval SYNCHRONOUSLY inside a wrappable, signature-resolvable method. Each entry names a readable METHOD; its owning class is resolved by that method's SIGNATURE (never the hashed class name), and the method is wrapped wrap-AROUND: the flag is set BEFORE the original runs and restored AFTER (in a finally, so it clears even if the original raises; nesting-safe). NB the street-tunnel walk is NOT such a case -- see the two disabled tunnelOut/tunnelIn entries: those readable methods only send a server b_set and the animation happens later in a HASHED handler, outside their window. The walk is handled by `spawn_context` (co_name) below. This section is kept for genuinely-synchronous spawners (and as approach-3 fallback: put a HASHED handler's own name here to resolve its class by that name's signature and wrap it wrap-around). method = readable method whose call brackets the interval creation; factor/group as for entries; enabled:false skips it.

closeBook-<doId>. factor 100 = effectively INSTANT (sub-frame) per user request -- book snaps closed, no animation.
the screen IRIS -- confirmed live to be the zone/tunnel/door transition (the circular iris that closes on every zone change; captured frame-by-frame on a tunnel entry). Intact literal name.

NAME-based fallback for any interval literally named '...tunnel...'. NB the actual street-tunnel WALK is NOT caught here -- its interval is auto-named 'vlt8e0d5a85-<n>' (confirmed live: this entry produced NO [SCALED] on a tunnel walk). The walk is now scaled by OBJECT IDENTITY (`tunnel_identity` below: it IS localAvatar.tunnelTrack), NOT by name. Kept intact in case a tunnel-named interval ever appears.

cog-battle FACEOFF (taunt-stare + walk-to-spots): faceoff-battle<id>. Discovered live from other players' fights via the global hook -- CLIENT-side movie visual only; damage/timers stay server-authoritative.

DISABLED on purpose. This is the mid-battle attack MOVIE (every attack + cog-death + dodge). Scaling it does NOT make combat faster and feels WORSE (confirmed live): the round is SERVER-gated (~13s fixed regardless of the client's early movieDone -- TTR deliberately ignores the early report), so speeding the movie just moves the ~3s of action earlier and leaves MORE of the fixed server wait as dead staring. Leaving the movie at normal speed lets the animation fill the server's round time instead. The battle INTRO (faceoff-battle + to-pending run-in) and OUTRO (movie-reward-track tally, client-driven) stay enabled -- those speedups work and are wanted; only this middle movie is dropped.
post-battle REWARD movie (gags/laff/jellybeans tally): movie-reward-track. Discovered live.

RUN-IN join walk (client-driven first round -> AI advances on d_joinDone, server timers are upper-bound fallbacks per STATUS): to-pending-toon. Discovered live. Matches open-toontown's iname_sub 'to-pending'.

context._note: DEPARTURE walk -- CONFIRMED WORKING LIVE. tunnelOut is readable, and tunnelOut -> b_setTunnelOut -> (local, synchronous) setTunnelOut -> handleTunnelOut -> self.tunnelTrack.start() all run in ONE synchronous call (b_ broadcasts set the value LOCALLY right away, then send to server). So the wrap-around context flag is still set when the walk Sequence starts, and it scales. (An earlier note here claimed this 'scales nothing' -- that was WRONG: I misread a log; the user confirmed the departure walk speeds up with exactly this.)

ARRIVAL walk -- best-effort. Symmetric to tunnelOut (tunnelIn -> b_setTunnelIn -> handleTunnelIn -> tunnelTrack.start(), synchronous on arrival), so context WOULD catch it -- BUT tunnelIn is hashed on this build, so resolving it by this readable name likely fails (the loader reports it unresolved and skips it: harmless no-op). If unresolved, arrival needs tunnelIn's hashed name (find via a LISTCLS of LocalToon or the co_name of the arrival walk) wired here.

_comment_spawn_context: SUPERSEDED for the tunnel walk by `tunnel_identity` (object identity of localAvatar.tunnelTrack) -- both tunnel spawn_context entries are now disabled (see their notes). The mechanism is kept intact (offline-validated, localtest/spawnctx_test.py) as a general tool for other fire-and-forget spawners. The `spawn_context` section scales an interval by the co_name of the Python FRAME THAT CALLED start() -- i.e. the (usually hashed) name of the method that spawned it. This is the fix for the street-tunnel WALK: the reference open-toontown LocalToon.handleTunnelIn/handleTunnelOut build an UNNAMED `self.tunnelTrack = Sequence(...)` (auto-named 'vlt8e0d5a85-<n>' on TTR, unmatchable by name) and immediately `.start()` it. Since start()'s wrapper is a native C trampoline (pushes no Python frame), tstate->frame at scale-time IS that handler frame; reading tstate->frame->f_code->co_name (PyThreadState.frame +0x18 -> PyFrameObject.f_code +0x20 -> PyCodeObject.co_name +0x70, CPython 3.8 ABI, offline-verified) yields the spawning function's name. An interval whose spawning co_name EXACTLY equals an entry's `co_name` is setPlayRate'd by that entry's factor -- exact match, so ONLY intervals spawned by a named function are touched and a hashed co_name (unique to its source) collides with nothing. co_name = the (hashed) spawning-method name; factor/group as for entries; enabled:false skips one. DISCOVERY: handleTunnelOut/handleTunnelIn are HASHED on TTR, so their real co_names are unknown until observed. Run one live tunnel walk with logging on -- every unmatched interval's DISTINCT spawning co_name is printed as [SPAWNCO] <co_name>; a NEW co_name appears exactly when you walk a tunnel (that is the hashed handler). Paste it into an entry's `co_name`. Best case (co_names not obfuscated) the readable guesses below already match on the first walk.
_comment_tunnel_localtoon_iris: PRIMARY tunnel-ARRIVAL mechanism (2026-09-06) -- DETERMINISTIC, no hardcoded per-session hash. The ARRIVAL walk is built + started by the HASHED handler handleTunnelIn, which is a METHOD OF THE LocalToon CLASS. LocalToon resolves RELIABLY by the `tunnelOut` method signature (unique -> class vlt725d40df) even though its module/class name is hashed. So: resolve LocalToon once, cache the SET of its OWN method names (tp_dict keys -- this set includes handleTunnelIn/handleTunnelOut under WHATEVER hash they got this session, because the obfuscator renames a `def NAME`'s co_name and its class-attribute key identically), and in the MetaInterval.start wrap-after scale any interval that (1) started within the iris window -- handleTunnelIn calls base.transitions.irisIn synchronously right before starting the walk, stamped as lastIrisMs -- AND (2) whose SPAWNING-FRAME co_name is a member of that LocalToon method set. Both gates are required, so it can NEVER hit MMO-noise walks (spawned by OTHER classes: other players' DistributedToon, cogs, NPCs -> co_name not in the set) or non-tunnel LocalToon animations (emotes etc. -> no iris). Teleport is name-matched by `entries` and returns first; the DEPARTURE is caught by the `context` tunnelOut wrap-around and returns first -> the arrival is the interval this catches, with no double-scale. This is why hardcoding a co_name (spawn_context, now retired) could never work: the post-iris co_names differ every session (playground animation noise) and the hash is per-build -- but the LocalToon method SET is re-derived live each session, so the current handleTunnelIn hash is always in it. lt_signature = the readable method(s) that uniquely resolve LocalToon (default ["tunnelOut"]); factor = speed multiplier; iris_window_ms = max ms between the iris start and the walk start; enabled:false turns it off. Env overrides: TTRMOD_TUNNEL_LT=0 (disable) / TTRMOD_TUNNEL_LT_FACTOR / TTRMOD_TUNNEL_LT_WINDOW_MS / TTRMOD_TUNNEL_LT_SIG. Offline-validated in localtest/ltiris_test.py; scales [SCALED] <name> x<factor> (tunnel) via=localtoon-method co=<hash>.
_comment_tunnel_identity: SECONDARY / fallback tunnel-walk mechanism (object identity). SUPERSEDED as the arrival path by `tunnel_localtoon_iris` above, which runs FIRST -- this depends on resolving base.localAvatar, which is ABSENT on TTR even in-world (the local toon lives in the client-repo object table behind hashed names), so it is a no-op live; kept enabled + offline-validated (localtest/tunnelident_test.py) as a fallback in case a build ever exposes localAvatar. The street-tunnel WALK is the interval `localAvatar.tunnelTrack` -- an UNNAMED Sequence (auto-named vlt8e0d5a85-<n>) that the HASHED handlers handleTunnelOut/handleTunnelIn build and .start(), stored under a HASHED attr. It matches no `entries` name and its spawning co_name is hashed, so it is identified by OBJECT IDENTITY: in the MetaInterval.start wrap-after, the starting interval IS localAvatar.<tunnelAttr>. `attr` null => auto-discover the hashed attr on the first iris-correlated walk (handleTunnelIn calls base.transitions.irisIn synchronously right before start(), so an irisTask fires in the same handler/frame window) then PIN it in memory, so every later walk scales in BOTH directions by identity alone -- and it can NEVER hit the teleport self.track (that interval is name-matched by `entries` and is under a different attr). Set `attr` to the value logged as [TUNNELATTR] to pin it up front and skip discovery. factor = speed multiplier; iris_window_ms = how tight the iris<->walk temporal correlation must be for discovery; enabled:false turns the whole tunnel-identity path off. Env overrides: TTRMOD_TUNNEL_ATTR / TTRMOD_TUNNEL_FACTOR / TTRMOD_IRIS_WINDOW_MS / TTRMOD_TUNNEL=0.

spawn_context._note: RETIRED / WRONG TARGET (disabled for the record). This Place-FSM 'Leaving' co_name DID spawn a localAvatar Sequence on tunnel departure, but it was a CAMERA / SETUP track (e.g. the tunnelOutLerpCamPos cam lerp or a scene-setup Sequence), NOT the toon-movement walk -- scaling it produced no visible faster walk. The earlier guess vlt749335ec was likewise WRONG: it scaled an unrelated walk interval, no tunnel effect. Both are superseded by `tunnel_identity` above (OBJECT IDENTITY of localAvatar.tunnelTrack), which targets the movement track itself. Kept here only to document what NOT to use.

RETIRED / WRONG + UNSTABLE (disabled for the record). This was a HARDCODED guess at the hashed handleTunnelIn co_name, captured once by [SPAWNCO]-after-irisTask. It CANNOT work: the post-iris co_names differ EVERY session because the playground is full of OTHER players' animations (MMO noise), and a hashed co_name is per-build anyway -- so no fixed hash can identify the arrival handler. Every such guess (vlt0de2d32e, vlt89637416, enterLeaving, vlt749335ec...) was wrong or unstable. The ARRIVAL is now scaled DETERMINISTICALLY by `tunnel_localtoon_iris` below: resolve LocalToon by the tunnelOut signature, cache its OWN method set (which includes the hashed handleTunnelIn THIS session), and scale any iris-correlated interval spawned by a member of that set -- no hardcoded hash. Kept here only to document what NOT to use.
